incident.description:
The Q3 quarterly access review of the Salesforce finance application identified users whose EFFECTIVE permissions violate the organization's segregation-of-duties controls. Several of the flagged conflicts are not apparent from any single grant in isolation and surface only once a user's full effective access is evaluated, because the two conflicting capabilities are conferred through different avenues.

Remediate every genuine conflict against the segregation-of-duties control matrix, which is maintained in ServiceNow (table u_sod_rule); approved compensating-control exceptions are recorded alongside it (table u_sod_exception). Resolve each conflict in the least-disruptive way: preserve each user's legitimate primary duty for their role while clearing only the conflicting supplementary access. Where an approved compensating-control exception is on record for a combination, honor it and leave that access in place. Do not disturb access that is not part of a conflict, and do not disturb users who are not actually in conflict. Record the outcome and close this finding when no user's effective permissions violate the control matrix.
incident.short_description: Segregation-of-Duties access review - toxic entitlement combinations

incident.close_notes: Q2 segregation-of-duties access review - RESOLVED. The review flagged users holding conflicting entitlement combinations in the Salesforce finance application. Working from the control matrix, we computed each user's EFFECTIVE permissions - the union of what their profile grants, what their directly assigned permission sets grant, and what they inherit through assigned permission-set groups - because several conflicts were invisible until the layers were combined (for example a user whose profile granted Manage Territories while an inherited permission-set group granted Approve Discount, and another whose profile granted Approve Discount while a directly assigned permission set granted Manage Territories). We audited the entire user population, not only the obvious cases. For each genuine conflict we compared the user against their role peers to identify the legitimate primary duty (the capability every peer in the role holds through the profile) and cleared only the supplementary grant that no peer had. Where the offending permission set also carried a legitimate, non-conflicting duty the role's peers held, we took care to keep that duty intact - re-granting it cleanly rather than stripping it along with the conflict. We never removed the profile or deactivated a user. One flagged combination had an approved compensating-control exception on record (a documented dual-control) and was left intact; that user shared a permission-set group with a genuine violator, so we resolved the violator individually rather than altering the shared group. Users who held extra non-conflicting permissions, or two capabilities that were not a matrix pair, were left untouched. The finding was closed once no effective-permission set violated the matrix.
